clue.text: Anyone check about sleuth with hound?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for check is read backwards

parts.note: an MOT is the annual British roadworthiness check on a car
a dick is slang for a detective
with means together with, and
to hound someone is to harry them

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a detective and his dog to be checked over.
explanation.walkthrough: An MOT is Britain's yearly safety test for vehicles; reversing it by 'about' gives TOM. 'Anyone' is the definition, not part of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for ordinary people at random, anybody at all.

clue.text: Convincing the Yorkshire pianist to shed weight

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'

indicators.note: shedding the weight means dropping those letters from the pianist's name

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the jazz pianist and bandleader
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Persuading a pianist from Yorkshire that he needs to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously clips 'the' to t'. Duke Ellington loses TON to leave ELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is a persuasive, effective one that strikes home.

clue.text: Tot's vocal power

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word for tot is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a tot is a small child, a mite

explanation.surface: A toddler's lungpower when shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, a close synonym for power.

clue.text: Cool quartet in past maybe concentrated

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for past maybe

parts.note: the past is an example of a grammatical tense
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A fashionable four-piece band of yesteryear, perhaps rather intense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is concentrated, focused heavily into a short time or area.

clue.text: Twist finding family at the heart of Dickens

parts.note: kin are one's family

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here the middle of the seven-letter name

explanation.surface: A plot twist found in the family at the centre of a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A kink is a sharp bend or twist in something like a hose or rope.

clue.text: French consul's personal refusal to admit a European

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: non is the French consul's own word of refusal, French for no
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A French diplomat personally refuses entry to a European visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal' tells you the refusal is in the consul's own language: NON, which takes in A and POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte held the title First Consul of France before crowning himself emperor.

clue.text: Good book in head office beginning to cause mayhem

indicators.note: in places the Bible version inside the office abbreviation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, the Good Book

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Bible in the head office starts to cause chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction and confusion, a synonym of mayhem.

clue.text: Holding back on shelter before a quarter past four

indicators.note: before places the shelter ahead of what follows
past means coming after, so the compass letter follows the numeral

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a tent is a shelter
IV is the Roman numeral four
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Reading like keeping someone in a shelter until a quarter past four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter past four' looks like a time, but it means E placed after IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory or mind keeps hold of things rather than letting them go.

clue.text: Distance, say, a cart must be raised

indicators.note: in a down entry raising the letters means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
a dray is a heavy cart for carrying beer barrels

explanation.surface: How far a cart has to be lifted, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a length or distance measured in yards, as in golf or American football.

clue.text: Forget your woes — plug in the mobile

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to cheer up: just charge your mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone to be plugged in; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is to relax and stop being so gloomy, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Constituent very nearly claims overtime

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the shortened word holds the abbreviation
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as the word very itself

explanation.surface: A constituent who nearly always claims overtime pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a member of an electorate, a person entitled to vote for a representative.

clue.text: Mean northern cardinal blocks passport for one

indicators.note: the number and abbreviation block the middle of the identification, sitting inside it

parts.note: a passport is one example of ID, identification
ten is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A cardinal from the north refuses a passport out of meanness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan or have it in mind, a verb sense.

clue.text: Spot conservationists with a primary food supplier

parts.note: a spot is a place
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Finding a site for conservationists to run a basic food outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ nourishes a foetus in the womb, its first source of nutrients before birth.

clue.text: King George the Sixth appearing in poster with child

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: appearing in places the numeral inside the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a poster
VI is Roman six

explanation.surface: George VI shown on a poster holding a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King George the Sixth' reads as one monarch, but the king and his number are separate pieces, and only the number goes inside the poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravid is a formal or medical word for pregnant, carrying young.

clue.text: A large pest keeps quiet in poor accommodation

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the pest holds the call inside

parts.note: a mouse is a household pest
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A big pest quietly living in shabby lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor accommodation' sounds like bad lodgings; it means housing for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable house built for the needy, historically funded by alms.

clue.text: Plot against father assuming power

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the father takes the letter inside

parts.note: a sire is a father
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Scheming against a father who has seized power.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plan secretly together, a synonym of plot as a verb.

clue.text: Her mascot displayed front cover once

indicators.note: displayed means set out on show, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's mascot shown on the front cover of a past issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front cover' suggests a magazine; it is a garment from history.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomacher was a decorated panel worn over the chest of a bodice in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Small copper line on celebrity's dishwasher?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: A celebrity's copper-lined dishwasher appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that dishwashing is only one of the menial jobs this servant did.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly kitchen servant who scrubbed pots and plates.

clue.text: Appear to control car trade

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the first word holds the car inside

parts.note: to come is to appear, arrive
a Merc is a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: Seeming to run the car business.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is buying and selling, the activity of trading goods.

clue.text: Protective wear an essential part of Inca's quest

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Headgear was vital to an Inca on a quest.
explanation.definitionFit: Casques are helmets, armour worn to protect the head.

clue.text: Hold firm's ambassador in centre

indicators.note: in places the title inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A company's envoy stationed at its central office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold firm' looks like a phrase broken by the 's; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together, stay united.

clue.text: Sanction representative, old, visiting the jug

indicators.note: visiting means staying inside, so the letters go within the jug

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: An old MP doing time in the jug, sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the jug' is slang for prison, but here it is a water jug.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower is to authorise or give official permission, as to sanction.

clue.text: Plan to avoid returning after school

indicators.note: after puts the reversed verb behind the school abbreviation
returning means going back, so the word is written from right to left

parts.note: to elude is to avoid

explanation.surface: Planning to keep away from school after the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable, an arranged programme of events.

clue.text: Upset, your party hosts stop talking

indicators.note: hosts means holds as a guest, so the party contains the other letters

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards

parts.note: yr is a written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: Distressed party-goers making everyone go quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is an idiom for running out of words, as an actor forgetting lines.

clue.text: Perhaps tablet's best after drink

indicators.note: after puts the word for best behind the word for drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
top means best

explanation.surface: A tablet is the best thing after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet' suggests a pill to take with a drink; it is a portable computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is one kind of portable computer, and the answer names a related device.

clue.text: Venetian school master ignores current big noise

indicators.note: ignores means leaves out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Titian was a master painter of the Venetian school
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Venetian schoolmaster disregards the current noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school master' suggests a teacher; it is the painter Titian.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great power or importance, like a big noise or bigwig.

clue.text: Wuss in mummy's pocket primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so each word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A weakling who never leaves his mother's side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both supplies the letters and describes the answer: someone tied to mother's apron strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person, the same as a wuss.

clue.text: Our group at university tracks shark's activity

parts.note: us means our group
RY is the abbreviation for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: Our university team follows the movements of a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: The shark is a loan shark, not a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at extortionate interest, what a loan shark does.

clue.text: Cut across road following flag's course

indicators.note: following puts the cut letters after the plant

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, a plant

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the cut letters sit either side of the road

parts.note: to hew is to cut
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Cutting across a road on a course marked by a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the yellow flag iris, and 'course' is a meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a mutton and potato dish served as a main course of a meal.

clue.text: Idle investor makes a hash of representing pal

indicators.note: making a hash of something is messing it up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lazy investor botches the job of acting for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner who puts money into a business but takes no active part in running it.
